geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the bent dominant mass in a courtyard macro to establish the required public void and active ground threshold.
Keep the void substantial enough to read as public space.
Align the courtyard opening to the access side to repair the frontage relation.
Make the courtyard-wrapped mass the root so the public void becomes the dominant organizational gesture.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the current cap logic into a courtyard organizer so the mass can open a public void rather than remain a sealed stacked block.
Size the court as a usable public subtraction instead of a decorative notch.
Open the court toward the verified access side in the program frame so the ground edge becomes legible and public.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent single mass across views and the bent/stepped roofline is legible, but it behaves mainly as a generic stacked block with a cantilevered cap. It responds weakly to the parcel and does not establish a meaningful public void or terrace at the verified access edge; the thick blue frontage reads as adjacent rather than actively addressed. Because the program is neighborhood living with an active ground threshold, one clear public void, and calm upper massing, this form is not yet program-fit: the ground plane is sealed, the void logic is absent, and the section does not yet support a convincing public/private hierarchy. Repair integrity is strong because the geometry is continuous and not visibly colliding, but the mass needs a carved court or entry seam aligned to the access side to become semantically appropriate.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more articulated and publicly porous than the candidate; it supports active edge logic but not the candidate's sealed courtless base.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact street-facing massing with a readable upper-volume shift and a protected ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Candidate lacks a legible carved public void and instead reads as a stacked block.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard/void as the primary organizer of the public experience, with mass wrapped around an open center.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a space-oriented reference; its lesson is threshold and sequence, not the candidate's exterior mass shape.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interior-scale threshold clarity and compact mass hierarchy can support a neighborhood program.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Tower language is only loosely relevant; candidate should not drift toward a tall office typology.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Ground articulation beneath a larger upper mass can preserve hierarchy and public interface.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A bridged/linear public passage can clarify a pedestrian edge through separation rather than enclosure.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable in the visible diagram, so the failure is semantic rather than containment-based.
The access edge is not answered by a legible public threshold; the form reads as turned away from the frontage.
Do not treat the stepped roof as a sufficient program section; it lacks public/occupied consequence.
